description: Composite six-panel figure of tensile-test data for a hot-rolled and intercritically annealed low-density medium-Mn steel; every panel is a line plot. (A1) Engineering stress-strain curves, Stress (MPa) 0-800 vs Strain (%) 0-14. (A2) True stress-strain curves, True stress (MPa) 0-800 vs True strain 0.00-0.12. Both A panels carry the identical legend: HR (gold), IA750_5 Min (green), IA750_30 Min (red), IA750_60 Min (black), IA750_120 Min (purple), IA750_180 Min (blue). (B1)-(B4) are work-hardening-rate (WHR) plots, Work hardening rate (MPa) vs True strain, for IA750_5 Min (0-4000 MPa, strain to 0.05), IA750_30 Min (0-6000, to 0.08), IA750_60 Min (0-6000, to 0.12) and IA750_180 Min (0-6000, to 0.05); each is annotated with blue dashed vertical dividers separating stage S1 (sharp initial drop) from the longer, oscillating stage S2. In (A1) the HR curve is shortest and highest (stresses above the 600 MPa gridline, ending before 2 % strain), whereas IA750_60 Min extends furthest, to about 12.5 % strain, and all annealed curves lie below HR in stress. (A2) preserves the same ranking in true coordinates. The group demonstrates that 60 min intercritical annealing yields the best strength-ductility balance and that the WHR level of stage S2 tracks that balance.

subfigures.description: Engineering stress-strain curves: Stress (MPa) 0-800 on the y-axis vs Strain (%) 0-14 on the x-axis, with six colour-coded curves (HR gold, IA750_5 Min green, IA750_30 Min red, IA750_60 Min black, IA750_120 Min purple, IA750_180 Min blue). HR terminates first at the highest stress; IA750_60 Min reaches the largest strain.

True stress-strain curves: True stress (MPa) 0-800 vs True strain 0.00-0.12, same six-colour legend. HR peaks near 0.015 true strain; IA750_60 Min extends to about 0.115 true strain at the top of the stress range.

Work hardening rate (MPa, 0-4000) vs True strain (0.00-0.05) for IA750_5 Min (red curve). Blue dashed vertical markers at about 0.015 and 0.044 true strain delimit stages labelled S1 and S2; WHR falls steeply then fluctuates at low values.
Work hardening rate (MPa, 0-6000) vs True strain (0.00-0.08) for IA750_30 Min (red). S1/S2 dividers near 0.019 and 0.065 true strain; stage S2 oscillates around higher values than in (B1).
Work hardening rate (MPa, 0-6000) vs True strain (0.00-0.12) for IA750_60 Min (red). S1/S2 dividers near 0.015 and 0.11 true strain; the longest and highest-lying stage S2 of the four WHR panels.
Work hardening rate (MPa, 0-6000) vs True strain (0.00-0.05) for IA750_180 Min (red). S1/S2 dividers near 0.016 and 0.045 true strain; the curve plunges below zero at the end of S2.

observations.observation: (A1) plots Stress (MPa) on a 0-800 axis against Strain (%) on a 0-14 axis and contains six labelled curves: HR, IA750_5 Min, IA750_30 Min, IA750_60 Min, IA750_120 Min and IA750_180 Min.
In (A1) the HR (gold) curve is the shortest, terminating before 2 % strain while still rising, at stresses above the 600 MPa gridline.
In (A1) the IA750_60 Min (black) curve extends furthest, to roughly 12-12.5 % strain, and lies highest among all annealed curves beyond about 6 % strain.
In (A1) the IA750_120 Min (purple) and IA750_180 Min (blue) curves terminate earliest among the annealed specimens, at roughly 4.5-5 % strain, with the lowest stress levels of the group.
(A2) plots True stress (MPa) 0-800 against True strain 0.00-0.12 with the same six curves; HR ends near 0.015 true strain and IA750_60 Min reaches about 0.115 true strain.
Panels (B1)-(B4) are work hardening rate curves with Work hardening rate (MPa) on the y-axis and True strain on the x-axis; the y-axis top tick is 4000 MPa in (B1) and 6000 MPa in (B2)-(B4).
Each WHR panel is divided by blue dashed vertical markers into a steeply falling initial stage labelled S1 and a longer, oscillating stage labelled S2.
The highest true strain reached in the WHR panels increases in the order IA750_5 Min (~0.045) < IA750_180 Min (~0.045) < IA750_30 Min (~0.065) < IA750_60 Min (~0.11).

The caption states that (A1) is the engineering stress-strain curve, (A2) the true stress-strain curve, and (B1)-(B4) the working hardening rate curves of intercritical annealed at 750 °C for 5, 30, 60 and 180 minutes respectively.
The citing text states the HRQ sample has the highest yield strength (486±6 MPa), highest ultimate tensile strength (674±20 MPa) and lowest total elongation (1.5±0.5 %).
The citing text states IA750_60 Min reaches a UTS of 658.45±6 MPa with a maximum total elongation of 12±0.95 %, attributed to optimum stability of reverted austenite and an enhanced TRIP effect.
The citing text reports mean stage-S2 work hardening rates of 1100-400 MPa for IA750_5 Min, 1700-1000 MPa for IA750_30 Min, 2000-1000 MPa for IA750_60 Min and 1500-900 MPa for IA750_180 Min.

The citing text assigns stage S1 to the sharply decreasing deformation of δ-ferrite and stage S2 to a near-linear decline caused by simultaneous softening and hardening (TRIP) during cooperative deformation of intercritical ferrite/untransformed austenite and reverted austenite.
The citing text notes that the large drop in properties at 120 minutes is linked to microstructural analysis in Fig. 4D2, which is not part of this figure group.

unreadable_items: Exact numerical endpoints of the individual stress-strain curves cannot be read precisely; they are given only as gridline ranges.
The (B1) y-axis top tick label is partially cut off at the panel border (bottom panel image), so only 4000 MPa is clearly legible.
